shortDescription: US–Iran fighting intensified and oil approached $96. Gold responded by falling for a fourth session.📉 Gold loses a major trend line🛢️ Conflict produces the wrong haven trade👷 Jobs data holds the escape route

children: US–Iran fighting intensified and oil approached $96. Gold responded by falling for a fourth session.
Gold loses a major trend line
Spot gold
fell 0.7% to slide under $4,300 Wednesday, its lowest level in more than three weeks. US futures dropped 1% to roughly $4,351.
Bullion has now declined for four consecutive sessions after trading near a three-month high
The selloff accelerated after gold broke below its 200-day moving average near $4,530. This indicator smooths approximately ten months of prices and helps traders identify the long-term trend.
Falling beneath it encouraged systematic and technical sellers to join an already uncomfortable retreat.

Immediate support sits around the psychological $4,300 level, followed by $4,250 and $4,200. Resistance appears near $4,400, while reclaiming the 200-day average would require a much larger recovery toward $4,530. The chart has moved from gentle pullback to fairly formal technical warning.
Conflict produces the wrong haven trade
US and Iranian forces exchanged fresh strikes while attacks on commercial tankers threatened supplies through the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude approached $96 and WTI crossed $91.
Normally, geopolitical escalation supports gold — but this conflict is reaching bullion through inflation and interest rates first.

The US ten-year Treasury yield rose above 4.81%, its highest since November 2023. Gold pays no interest, so rising bond yields increase its “opportunity cost” — the return investors sacrifice by holding bullion instead of an income-producing asset.
The dollar index climbed toward 99.8, its strongest level in roughly two weeks. A firmer dollar makes gold more expensive for buyers using other currencies.
That leaves bullion squeezed between attractive US yields and a strengthening currency, despite offering its usual résumé of inflation protection and crisis insurance.
Jobs data holds the escape route
Markets now price roughly a 67% probability of a September Fed rate increase, up from about 40% one week ago.
Fed boss Kevin Warsh and other officials have signaled willingness to tighten if inflation persists. Oil’s latest surge has made that warning considerably less theoretical.
ADP private-payroll figures arrive Wednesday before Friday’s
Weak hiring could lower yields and reduce rate-hike expectations, offering gold some relief. Strong jobs data would support the Fed’s case and risk extending the slide deeper beneath $4,300.

Silver fell 1% toward $63.60, while platinum and palladium also weakened. Safe-haven demand is still there, but until interest-rate pressure eases, buyers are attempting to catch something considerably heavier than a falling knife.
Gold can’t find the floor
Prices cut through $4,300
Inflation, bond jitters surface

title: XAU/USD: Gold Slides Below 200-Day Average as Yields Defeat Safe-Haven Demand
